name: Queenstown
title: Holidays in Queenstown
intro: Jet boats, a luge with a lake view and Milford Sound up the road. Here's what Queenstown is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 11 to 13 hrs ahead of the UK

facts_note: The NZeTA comes with a visitor levy, both paid online. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: December to March is summer, with long days for lakes and hiking. June to September is ski season on four nearby mountains. April's autumn colours are lovely and quieter.

things.name: Skyline gondola and luge
things.blurb: Ride up, then race down on a luge track. Children always want one more go.

things.name: Shotover Jet
things.blurb: A fast jet boat spinning through a narrow canyon.

things.name: Milford Sound
things.blurb: Fiords and waterfalls on a cruise. A long day by road, or fly.

things.name: TSS Earnslaw
things.blurb: A 100-year-old steamship across the lake to a sheep farm.

things.name: Kiwi Birdlife Park
things.blurb: See real kiwis in a nocturnal house.

things.name: Queenstown Gardens
things.blurb: Lakeside gardens with a playground and frisbee golf.

faqs.question: Is Queenstown good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, as part of a New Zealand trip. It's packed with activities, and many suit younger children. The thrill rides have height limits.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Five to seven nights, within a New Zealand trip of three weeks or more.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, but British passport holders need an NZeTA, applied for online, and pay a visitor levy. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: How do you get there?
faqs.answer: Fly via Auckland, Sydney or Melbourne. The whole journey takes around 30 hours, so a stopover helps.
